title: Nine slow nights in the tea valleys
start: NJP railway station or Bagdogra airport
end: NJP railway station or Bagdogra airport

cost_split.item: Shared jeeps, local jeeps and four reserved car transfers
Homestays and hotels, 9 nights, mostly with dinner and breakfast

meta_description: 9 slow nights in the tea valleys from ₹31,000: Kurseong, two nights at Makaibari, Sittong, Latpanchar hornbills and Mirik, on jeeps and homestays.
summary: Our longest trip in the land, at a walking pace. Two nights each in Kurseong, a Makaibari tea family, Sittong and Mirik, and one at Latpanchar for hornbills. Mostly homestays and shared jeeps, with cars only where there is no other way. From about ₹31,000 per person.
intro: This trip is for people with time who want to know a place rather than tick it off. Nine nights let you settle into each stop: a town, a tea garden, an orange village, a forest village and a lake. You eat with families most nights and learn more from them than from any sight.

We keep costs down with shared jeeps where they run and village homestays with meals, and use a reserved car only for the cross-country legs that have no regular transport. The pace is relaxed; most days have one main activity and plenty of time to rest.
highlights: Two nights with a Makaibari tea family
Netaji's house and the toy train bazaar
Sittong's orchards and the Riyang river

days.title: Siliguri to Kurseong
days.text: Take a shared jeep up to Kurseong and settle into a homestay. Walk the bazaar in the afternoon, watch for the toy train, and eat momos by the station.

days.title: Netaji's house and Dow Hill
days.text: Climb Eagle's Crag at dawn, then visit Netaji's house at Giddapahar. In the afternoon, walk up the Dow Hill forest road to the old schools and back, about 3 hours.

days.title: Down to Makaibari
days.text: Take a local jeep down the Pankhabari road to Makaibari and move in with your host family. Spend the afternoon walking the village and the edge of the garden, and help in the kitchen if you are invited.

days.title: Plucking, factory and tasting
days.text: Walk out with the pluckers at dawn. Later, visit the factory if it is working and taste first, second and autumn flush side by side. In the afternoon, walk the forest paths between the estate villages with a young guide.

days.title: Over the ridge to Sittong
days.text: Drive up through Kurseong and over the Bagora ridge, stopping at Chimney, then down into the Riyang valley to Sittong. Walk the orchards in the afternoon.

days.title: The Riyang river and the church
days.text: Walk down to the Riyang river with a packed lunch and climb back by mid-afternoon. In the evening, visit the old church and buy oranges from a grower in season.

days.title: Namthing Pokhri to Latpanchar
days.text: Drive to Namthing Pokhri, the salamander lake, and walk its edge quietly. Continue to Latpanchar, check in, and walk through the cinchona plantations in the afternoon with your host.

days.title: Hornbill dawn, then Mirik
days.text: Go out at dawn with a bird guide for hornbills, or drive up to Ahaldara for sunrise. After breakfast, take a reserved car down towards the plains and up the Dudhia road to Mirik, stopping at Tingling and Sourenee. Walk the lake in the evening.

days.title: Mirik lake and Bokar Monastery
days.text: Walk round Sumendu Lake at dawn, then climb to Bokar Monastery for prayers and Rameetay Dara for the view. Spend the afternoon on the tea and orange slopes around town.

days.title: Mirik to Siliguri
days.text: Take a morning shared jeep from Mirik to Siliguri and continue to NJP or Bagdogra. Keep a buffer of three hours for traffic.

includes: Jeeps and reserved cars as listed
Homestays and mid-range rooms on twin sharing
Dinner and breakfast at homestays; breakfast at hotels
excludes: Flights and trains to NJP or Bagdogra
save_money: Pool reserved cars with other travellers at your homestay for the cross-country legs.
Stay in homestays with meals included; restaurant dinners double the food budget.
Travel in the shoulder months of late September or February for lower rates.
good_to_know: Latpanchar to Mirik is the longest drive; start right after breakfast.
Mahananda sanctuary closes in the monsoon; forest trails at Latpanchar then shut.
Carry enough cash for village stops; ATMs are only in Kurseong and Mirik.

faqs.a: Yes. ₹31,000 is per person on twin sharing for Indian nationals, from NJP or Bagdogra and back, as an indicative 2025–26 figure. Solo travellers pay more for rooms and cars; groups of four sharing a car pay less. We round to the nearest ₹500.

faqs.q: Can we start from Bagdogra airport instead of NJP?
faqs.a: Yes. Bagdogra is about 30 minutes from Siliguri and a little further from NJP. Shared autos and taxis link the airport to the Siliguri jeep stands. With a reserved car, the fare from Bagdogra is about the same as from NJP.

faqs.q: Can we change the number of nights?
faqs.a: Yes. Add a night where you want more time, usually in the village stops, or drop one on a tight schedule. Keep at least two nights in any place where you want a clear dawn view, since weather can spoil one morning.

faqs.q: Who is this nine-night trip for?
faqs.a: Travellers with time who prefer depth to distance: retired couples, students on a break, writers, photographers and anyone who wants to live briefly in a tea garden and a farming village. If you want many sights, a shorter trip suits you better.

faqs.q: Can I do this trip without any reserved cars?
faqs.a: Mostly, but not completely. Shared jeeps cover Siliguri, Kurseong and Mirik well, but Makaibari to Sittong and Latpanchar to Mirik have no practical shared transport. Pooling a car with other guests is the cheapest solution.

faqs.q: Will I get bored in the villages?
faqs.a: Probably not, if you enjoy walking, reading, food and conversation. Each village stop has one main activity per day and lots of free time. Bring a book, binoculars and curiosity.

faqs.q: Is this trip possible in the monsoon?
faqs.a: Parts of it are, at lower prices, but Mahananda sanctuary closes, village roads become slippery and landslides can cut routes. If you come between June and September, keep flexible days and skip Latpanchar.

faqs.q: How much cash should I carry?
faqs.a: Enough for at least four or five days of village stays, homestay payments, guides and jeeps, since ATMs are only in Kurseong and Mirik. UPI works in many places but not all; carry cash as a back-up.

faqs.q: Can we shorten it to six nights?
faqs.a: Yes. Drop one night each at Kurseong, Makaibari and Sittong. You keep all the places but lose the slack days. Or follow our seven-night Comfort loop with homestays instead of hotels.
